findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There wasn't any soap available at the hand washing sink near the dish room. A new bag of soap was added to the soap dispenser to correct the violation. Ensure that there is always soap available at every handsink to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The chemical sanitizing dish machine was observed testing at 0ppm (CL). The machine was cycled and primed several times without a change in concentration. The facility was instructed to sanitize all dishes in triple sink until the dish machine can be serviced. Ensure that machine is serviced and sanitizing at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration. Will follow-up 6/15/2026.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: There were storage racks inside of the walk in cooler that contained a fuzzy debris on the outer surfaces. Shown to the PIC. Suggests that racks are taken outdoors to be power washed during down time. Ensure that racks are cleaned as frequently as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed there was not paper towels at the front hand washing sink (next to the custard preparation area) when the inspector arrived. Paper towels are required for the proper hand washing procedure. The PIC re-filled the paper towel dispenser during the inspection. Ensure that paper towels are always available at every hand washing sink.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the can opener blade had a buildup of debris when the inspector arrived. The inspector explained that food can become contaminated when blades are soiled. The PIC removed the can opener to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized during the inspection. Ensure that the can opener is always sanitized after use.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed there is a building of debris around the soda nozzles of the customer service drink station (the soda nozzles are clean; the buildup is only in the surrounding area). Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil resides. Ensure that the area around the soda nozzles are clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed the floor underneath the custard preparation station and the drive through station have an accumulation of food, garbage, dirt, and other debris. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of resides. Ensure that the floor underneath the custard station and drive through station are clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed the bottom of the prep cooler next to the dish machine was not holding temperature control for safety (TCS) foods at 41F or below. The ambient air temperature of the cooler was between 47F - 55F and the thermometer inside was reading about 48F. The foods inside the cooler were large containers of chicken strips, hot dogs, and chicken patties. The internal temperature of the chicken strips were 48F, hotdogs were 47F, and chicken patties were 50F. All of the foods had been inside the cooler since this morning. The foods were voluntarily discarded during the inspection. There were no other foods inside the prep cooler. For information about the cooler see violation #33.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Observed the bottom of the prep cooler next to the dish machine was not holding foods at 41F or below. There was not any foods held in the top of the prep cooler since it is known to be broken by the PIC. The PIC was not aware the bottom was also not functioning. The PIC stated that service was already in the process of being scheduled for the top of the prep cooler. Both the top and bottom will be serviced now. The inspector will return on 10/04/2024 to check on the temperature of the prep cooler. No TCS foods should be held inside the cooler until it is serviced and sufficient to cold hold foods at 41F or below. For information about the discarded foods see violation #22.

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the fans in the walk-in cooler have an accumulation of dust. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. Ensure the fans are cleaned by the next routine inspection. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed a mop being stored with the head in the mop sink basin. The mop was hung invented during the inspection. Ensure that mops are always stored in a position that allows the head to air dry.

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed almost all employees at the facility washing their hands improperly and none appeared to have an understanding of proper hand washing procedure. When asked about proper procedure person-in-charge was unaware of requirement to use a barrier to turn faucets off. Inspector scheduled assistance from the heatlh educator for hand washing education at the facility. Corrected by education, no follow-up required at this time. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Non-food-contact surfaces throughout the facility that are not in the open have begun to accumulate a heavy amount of soil including but not limited to shelving, the underside of shelving, rear surfaces of equipment, and the hood vent for the dish machine. Ensure that all non-food-contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned often enought to prevent the accumulation of debris and residue. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION.

All hard-to-reach areas of the facility require deep cleaning. Cleaning in genral areas appears excellent. Ensure that walls and floors behind and under equipment are clean to sight and touch and often enough to prevent the accumulation of residue and debris. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a mop being stored head down in the mop sink at the rear of the facility. Another mop was stored head down next to the mop sink. Ensure that mops are stored properly when they are not in use by hanging them inverted against the wall or resting within the top portion of a mop bucket to allow for drying and the prevention of microbial growth.

6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed debris behind the coolers, prep areas and custard machines at the front of the store. The debris was most significant in the far left corner when facing the coolers towards the vertical cooler. Ensure that areas which are not part of the standard cleaning practices are cleaned routinely to keep them clean and prevent contamination and buildup. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

On arrival, test strips are not available at the facility for the Quat sanitizer used in the sani bucket. A small amount was acquired during the inspection to correct the violation. PIC is instructed to ensure that a supply of test strips is always available for the sanitizers used in the facility.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

A thick accumulation of ice is observed on the shelves, packaged foods and floor under the cooling unit in the walk in freezer. Ice prevents effective cleaning. PIC instructed to maintain the freezer sufficiently clear of ice to facilitate effective cleaning. Inspector suggested some form of catch pan to contain the build up of ice. The catch pan (if used) will need to be cleaned regularly to prevent overflow.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Paper towels for men's bathroom empty. PIC will resupply bathroom. Reference 6-301.12.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed cheese to be measured at 108F (probed). Hot holding unit was unplugged. Ensure hot held food remain at or above 135F at all times. Corrected. Food was discarded. Machine was plugged in. Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed sanitizer bucket to be 0ppm. In addition, quat dispenser registered to be 0ppm. Upon further investigation, quat line had blockage preventing water and chemical to mix. Corrected. Quaternary chemical line was fixed and dispenser was fixed. All buckets were re-filled.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Quaternary ammonium sanitizer measured 0 ppm in sanitizer bucket. Maintain concentration indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed Prep line near handsink to be turned off. All foods were above 50F. Corrected. All TCS foods were discarded from cooler. This included tomatoes and sauces. Lettuce was just placed in cooler. PIC discovered prep cooler was turned off. Prep cooler was turned on.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Tomatoes, mayonaise, and other food items were above 50F. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly chilled to less than 41°F ***** discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Observed food debris in walk-in freezer. In addition, ice accumulation can be seen in walk-in cooler. Clean floor areas.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Reference 6-501.12

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-120(a) Observed two packages of burger patties stored in the prep cooler at the end of the cook line closest to the ware washing area to have an surface temperature of 64 F and internal temperatures of 52 F and 60 F . Cooler had an internal air temperature of approximately 80 F.  Management on-site stated that burgers were most likely placed in the cooler prior to lunch service at approximately 10 AM. Packages of patties were discarded to correct the violation. On-site management states that cooler ceased to properly function beginning Saturday (07/08/17) and that the facility's service providers have been contacted. Until unit has been repaired, facility shall not store TCS foods in this unit. All TCS food shall be stored at the proper temperature during storage.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: 750-540 Observed no FSSMCs on-site during routine inspection. Management on-site states that three managers have been scheduled to complete a ServSafe mangers course in the next month. Inspector should be notified when managers have successfully completed course. All category I (high risk) facilities shall have adequate number of FSSMCs to cover all shifts.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-120(a), 750-130(b) Observed three boxes of french fries stored on the floor in the walk in freezer. Food employees state that a delivery was received at approximately 9 AM today. Food shall be stored at least six inches off the floor. Deliveries shall be scheduled for times when stock can be properly stored.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800(b) (1)Observed the slicer used for tomatoes and onions to be soiled with an accumulation of dried food debris. (2) Observed the can opener blade at the prep table in the dry storage area to be soiled with an accumulation of dried food debris. Food contact surfaces shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use to prevent potential contamination of food. Slicer and can opener blade were removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized during inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: 750-540 Observed no FSSMC available for the current shift. Facility management states that two food employees are attending an approved Serve Safe course next week to receive their FSSMC certification and intends to have a third food employee attend a course in the future. Additionally, facility management states that FSSMC for the current shift has recently left. Category I (high risk) facilities shall have adequate FSSMCs to cover all shifts. Educational material on applying for FSSMC certification online through IDPH was provided during inspection.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: (1) Observed cheese slices, cooked onions, and bacon stored in ice baths on cook line without lids during down time. (2) Observed sundae toppings including chocolate sauce, nuts, and cookie bits to be stored on the prep line without covers. Employee states that toppings are covered overnight and uncovered at approximately 8:30 AM for prep. Facility opens at 10:30 AM. Food shall be protected at all times during storage, service, and display. Provide a cover for food between prep and in-use periods to protect food from coughs, sneezes, or other sources of potential contamination. Covers were provided to correct the violation. 750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.750-130(a) Food shall be stored in clean, covered containers once being removed from the original package.750-130 Ready to eat food shall be stored in a matter to prevent cross-contamination.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: Observed the can opener blade on the prep table by the soda machine to be soiled with an accumulation of food debris and what appears to be mold. Clean and maintain food contact surfaces to prevent potential cross contamination.750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: (1) the interior of the cheese dispenser with food debris, (2) the shelves in the tray prep area with food debris, (3) the condiment wall dispensers with food debris, and (4) the shelving units in the walk in cooler with food debris. Clean and maintain non-food contact surfaces to prevent providing food, water, and harborage for pests.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: (1) Observed the floor underneath the dish machine to be soiled with food debris, dust, and ponding water. Drains covers were placed in a manner that was pouring water on the floor. Drain covers were corrected and water was mopped up to correct the violation. Ensure that drain covers are positioned correctly to properly drain wastewater. (2) Observed the floors under the shelving units in the walk in cooler to be soiled with food debris, ice, and soil. There is a build up of ice at the wall and door adjacent to the walk in cooler. Ice is not a cleanable surface. Remove ice routinely to provide a smooth, cleanable surface. Management states that the service provider for the unit will be contacted to determine the cause of the build up.750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: Observed the air vent in the ceiling over the prep table by the soda machine to be soiled with an accumulation of dust. Clean vent to prevent potential contamination of food prepared in this area. 750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.
